floors.description: A gorge country of blue crevasses, crossed by bridges of living ice that the trolls grow, own, and lease.   Every span has its bridge-troll and every bridge-troll has its price. The rates are fair. The exceptions are memorable.

monsters.name: Bridge-troll
monsters.lore: It doubled its rates for the season and glued the detour shut. The deed is in one fist, in case you argue.

monsters.name: Toll-runner wolf
monsters.lore: It crosses without paying and shakes the spans until paying customers fall off. The trolls call it undignified. It calls it lunch.

monsters.name: Crevasse climber
monsters.lore: Not everyone who fell short on the toll hit the bottom. It climbs with its grudge in both hands.

monsters.name: Gorge raven
monsters.lore: It nests under the spans and audits every crossing. Whatever falls, it files.

runt.tag: gaunt and limping — an easy kill, thin pickings

tough.tag: scarred and heavy-set — dangerous, but it will pay

alpha.tag: an alpha, twice the size — worth a fortune or a funeral

floors.description: Farms, if farms were built by things four men tall — fences of whole pines, cattle the size of barns. The frost giants hold these steadings as the Jarl's freeholders, and they do not care for trespass across land it takes a day to walk.

monsters.name: Freeholder giant
monsters.lore: The near field is posted and the post is the hammer. Freeholders this size do not lose arguments on their own land — they last them out.

monsters.name: Steading hound
monsters.lore: Bred to giant scale, it clears the pine fence without touching it. It is not angry. It is on the clock.

monsters.name: Rick-thief troll
monsters.lore: It was stealing hay until you arrived and became the better idea.

monsters.name: Steading bull
monsters.lore: Cattle bred for owners four men tall. It does not recognize fences, seasons, or you.

runt.tag: gaunt and limping — an easy kill, thin pickings

tough.tag: scarred and heavy-set — dangerous, but it will pay

alpha.tag: an alpha, twice the size — worth a fortune or a funeral

floors.description: The Jarl builds in ice the way kings below built in granite, and the blocks come from here — quarries cut in terraces into the glacier's blue heart. The deeper terraces are older than the Jarl, and their blocks were not left unfinished by accident.

monsters.name: Quarry-gang troll
monsters.lore: It works a two-troll saw alone, which is against the gang rules, which it ate.

monsters.name: Quarried thing
monsters.lore: The deep blocks were not left unfinished by accident. It has been sawing from its side, and it is nearly out.

monsters.name: Gantry wolf
monsters.lore: It patrols the top gantry like a foreman and comes down the ramps collecting the pack as it comes.

monsters.name: Quarry crow
monsters.lore: Every work site feeds its crows. This quarry's crows have opinions about who counts as site waste.

runt.tag: gaunt and limping — an easy kill, thin pickings

tough.tag: scarred and heavy-set — dangerous, but it will pay

alpha.tag: an alpha, twice the size — worth a fortune or a funeral

floors.description: A cataract of coolant, milk-white and dead cold, falling from a cracked main above the clouds and freezing as it lands — a waterfall growing its own mountain. The spray coats everything in white glass, and the locals chip their doors open every morning.

monsters.name: Glass-coat wolf
monsters.lore: Its coat of frozen coolant is white armor. It shatters its own casing to charge, and arrives in a burst of glass.

monsters.name: Falls troll
monsters.lore: It stands under the cataract for pleasure, growing a second hide. The silhouette under-promises.

monsters.name: White pilgrim
monsters.lore: People come to see the Falls, and some stand too long in the spray. This one is still patient under a finger of glass.

monsters.name: Ice marten
monsters.lore: It dens in the dry pocket behind the cataract and robs the viewing path at its leisure.

runt.tag: gaunt and limping — an easy kill, thin pickings

tough.tag: scarred and heavy-set — dangerous, but it will pay

alpha.tag: an alpha, twice the size — worth a fortune or a funeral

floors.description: The glacier funnels the floor's whole weather through one pass, and the wind through it has been sharpened for centuries. The Wind Walls break it — ramparts of ice block, slotted and singing. Crossings are done at a sprint, by bell signal, or not at all.

monsters.name: Wall-warden giant
monsters.lore: It leans into the gale holding a shield the size of a barn door — shelter for travelers, for a fee. You are past due.

monsters.name: Gale-running wolf
monsters.lore: It runs with the gale at its back and arrives at twice a wolf's honest speed. The bell rings once.

monsters.name: Shutter troll
monsters.lore: Paid in fish heads and deference. Today the shutters stay down, and its back is against them.

monsters.name: Gale kite
monsters.lore: It is the only thing that flies the pass by choice, and it uses the wind the way an angler uses a river.

runt.tag: gaunt and limping — an easy kill, thin pickings

tough.tag: scarred and heavy-set — dangerous, but it will pay

alpha.tag: an alpha, twice the size — worth a fortune or a funeral

floors.description: A processional road of fitted ice blocks, wide enough for six giants abreast, lit by whale-oil lamps that never gutter. The Jarl's own approach, swept daily, patrolled hourly. You are expected. That is not a comfort.

monsters.name: Thane of the road
monsters.lore: Custom entitles you to give your name and have it spoken at your defeat. The custom is observed; so is the plate.

monsters.name: Jarl's herald-wolf
monsters.lore: Whatever it reports back decides how much of the garrison you meet. It circles once, taking notes.

monsters.name: Lamplighter troll
monsters.lore: Nine generations of trolls have held the lamp post, all of them it. Brawling on the road is its second duty.

monsters.name: Post raven
monsters.lore: The Jarl's road-post flies ahead of every traveler. Interfering with the mail is a listed offense.

runt.tag: gaunt and limping — an easy kill, thin pickings

tough.tag: scarred and heavy-set — dangerous, but it will pay

alpha.tag: an alpha, twice the size — worth a fortune or a funeral

floors.description: The Jarl's citadel is a glacier carved into a mead-hall, rafters of blue ice, a fire-trench down the middle burning cold white. The tables are set for a thousand, and the thousand are here. The horn by the door is for challengers. It is not decorative.

monsters.name: Hall-thane
monsters.lore: It asked the room's leave to answer the horn, formally, and the room granted it like an avalanche starting.

monsters.name: Mead-bearer troll
monsters.lore: The barrel it set down was for you. It is not, now.

monsters.name: Hearth-wolf
monsters.lore: The Jarl's own, with first claim on challengers by right of seniority. No thane disputes it.

monsters.name: Ice skald
monsters.lore: It sings the hall's cold fire brighter, and verses this old shrug off newer magic.

runt.tag: gaunt and limping — an easy kill, thin pickings

tough.tag: scarred and heavy-set — dangerous, but it will pay

alpha.tag: an alpha, twice the size — worth a fortune or a funeral

floors.description: The stair opens onto open sky. Peaks rise out of a cloud deck that goes to every horizon, and the wind arrives with no memory of ever being stopped. The locals rope themselves to their own houses, and will lend you a line for a fair price.

monsters.name: Cloudline harpy
monsters.lore: The insults in fluent trade-tongue are a range-finding exercise. The stoop comes on the punchline.

monsters.name: Squall drake
monsters.lore: It has not learned to aim its lightning yet. It does not especially need to.

monsters.name: Fallen rigger
monsters.lore: It clips its frayed line to your belt with terrible courtesy. Its ship is down there somewhere, and it means to introduce you.

monsters.name: Cliff goat
monsters.lore: It holds the trail ledges against all comers, and the drop has never once been its problem.

runt.tag: gaunt and limping — an easy kill, thin pickings

tough.tag: scarred and heavy-set — dangerous, but it will pay

alpha.tag: an alpha, twice the size — worth a fortune or a funeral

floors.description: Sky-ships died here in numbers — a whole trade fleet, caught between the tower's theft and the storm it made. The hulls lie broken across three peaks, keels to the sky. Salvage is the floor's whole economy, and the previous owners have opinions.

monsters.name: Salvage harpy
monsters.lore: The clan matriarch wears three captains' coats at once. Everything on this peak is claimed, including, as of now, your gear.

monsters.name: Hold-nesting drake
monsters.lore: Brooding a clutch on a bed of trade silver — possessive, charged, and recently a parent.

monsters.name: Crew of the wreck
monsters.lore: They rise in harness and oilskin, moving with the roll of a deck that stopped rolling years ago.

monsters.name: Hull borer
monsters.lore: It ate through the fleet's timber for years and grew a back of lapped ship-iron doing it. Cutting it down is a shipwright's job, not a soldier's.

runt.tag: gaunt and limping — an easy kill, thin pickings

tough.tag: scarred and heavy-set — dangerous, but it will pay

alpha.tag: an alpha, twice the size — worth a fortune or a funeral

floors.description: Every ledge of these crags is built up with harpy nests — driftwood, rigging, one entire church roof — stacked into a city without streets. The harpies are not hostile so much as governed by an etiquette you cannot see, and the fines are paid in blood.

monsters.name: Rookery matron
monsters.lore: You walked under somebody's nest, which is either a toll or a proposal. She is here to settle which.

monsters.name: Fledgling mob
monsters.lore: Eleven of them, dared to touch you. The arithmetic of being twelve is the whole of harpy education.

monsters.name: Rookery drake
monsters.lore: Penned like a town bull, resented, and prayed to. The prayers soaked in; spells break against them.

monsters.name: Rook marten
monsters.lore: It raids the nests for eggs and trinkets, and it has learned to work while the owners are out on you.

runt.tag: gaunt and limping — an easy kill, thin pickings

tough.tag: scarred and heavy-set — dangerous, but it will pay

alpha.tag: an alpha, twice the size — worth a fortune or a funeral

floors.description: The chains that hold this realm into the tower run overhead — links the size of houses, climbing into cloud, humming with load. Whole communities live on the links, farming moss, netting birds. Twice a day the chains move a few feet. Everyone holds on.

monsters.name: Chain-walker harpy
monsters.lore: Flying here is for amateurs, she explains, kicking your handhold loose to illustrate the point.

monsters.name: Link-coiled drake
monsters.lore: Your footsteps carry up the chain like a knock. It pours down through the links, and it has never needed a floor.

monsters.name: Moss-farmer's remnant
monsters.lore: It missed a handhold years ago and still works its ledge, weightless-thin. The net it waves you toward is for you.

monsters.name: Chain tick
monsters.lore: It clamps to the great links and drinks the hum of the load. Its shell is chain-grade by adoption.

runt.tag: gaunt and limping — an easy kill, thin pickings

tough.tag: scarred and heavy-set — dangerous, but it will pay

alpha.tag: an alpha, twice the size — worth a fortune or a funeral

floors.description: Between two ranges the whole floor's air goes up. The locals ride barn-sized kites between the towns, and the wildlife has organized around the free lift. Nothing here fights on the ground if it can help it. You are the only thing that cannot help it.

monsters.name: Updraft duelist
monsters.lore: Three passes, honor satisfied — the local dueling form. Nobody has explained what satisfies it.

monsters.name: Kite-line cutter
monsters.lore: It drops travelers into the valley for the things below. You are not even attached to a line. Free lunch.

monsters.name: Column drake
monsters.lore: Asleep on the wind in the updraft's core. Your scent goes up the column ahead of you.

monsters.name: Pass boar
monsters.lore: The only local that never took the free lift. It holds the valley floor out of pure principle.

runt.tag: gaunt and limping — an easy kill, thin pickings

tough.tag: scarred and heavy-set — dangerous, but it will pay

alpha.tag: an alpha, twice the size — worth a fortune or a funeral

floors.description: A summit plateau where the fleet's masts were driven in like fence-posts — hundreds of them, full-rigged, sails long gone to harpy nests, shrouds still singing. Walking here means walking under a century of standing rigging. Look up more than you look down.

monsters.name: Shroud-runner harpy
monsters.lore: She runs the rigging without touching wing to air, herding you toward the net stretch where the clan waits.

monsters.name: Crowsnest drake
monsters.lore: Grown into the tallest crow's nest, spars through the wing membrane. It rings every stay on the way down.

monsters.name: Tangled topman
monsters.lore: A topman hanging where his line caught him. The swinging stops against the wind, and the line starts paying out.

monsters.name: Shroud crab
monsters.lore: It climbed up from some hold with the fleet and never left the rigging. The shell has out-lasted three hulls.

runt.tag: gaunt and limping — an easy kill, thin pickings

tough.tag: scarred and heavy-set — dangerous, but it will pay

alpha.tag: an alpha, twice the size — worth a fortune or a funeral

floors.description: A high moor where the storm grounds itself, all day, every day. The old folk farmed the lightning with copper poles, and the poles still stand, singing before every strike. The safe lanes are marked in white stone. The stones get moved. Not by the wind.

monsters.name: Charge-thief harpy
monsters.lore: She takes the strike across her banded feathers like applause. Spark-drunk, several strikes in, and spells just read as more applause.

monsters.name: Fieldborn drake
monsters.lore: Hatched on this moor and never left — why would it. Every pole it passes fires in salute.

monsters.name: Lane-stone mover
monsters.lore: The thing that moves the white lane-stones. Under the hood is old lightning, coiled and patient. It has been farming climbers.

monsters.name: Copper rat
monsters.lore: It gnaws the pole-farm's wiring for the taste and has been struck more times than the poles.

runt.tag: gaunt and limping — an easy kill, thin pickings

tough.tag: scarred and heavy-set — dangerous, but it will pay

alpha.tag: an alpha, twice the size — worth a fortune or a funeral

floors.description: The high crags belong to the storm drakes outright — aeries on every summit, each one a hoard of wreck-metal and old charge. The drakes keep the Queen's law as aristocrats keep any law. Climbers rank somewhere between trespass and sport.

monsters.name: Aerie heir
monsters.lore: Young enough to want a story worth telling, old enough to make one out of you.

monsters.name: Harpy drake-groom
monsters.lore: Drake-scale livery and airs to match. Removing you before the master wakes is the kind of initiative that gets noticed.

monsters.name: Deposed tyrant
monsters.lore: Beaten off its crag, wings scarred, charge gone grey. It has nothing left but seniority, and it means to spend it on you.

monsters.name: Hoard lizard
monsters.lore: It lives in the aeries' wreck-metal hoards and defends them harder than the owners do.

runt.tag: gaunt and limping — an easy kill, thin pickings

tough.tag: scarred and heavy-set — dangerous, but it will pay

alpha.tag: an alpha, twice the size — worth a fortune or a funeral

floors.description: The Queen's storm stands over the last peak like a crown, and this floor is its wall — a ring of black weather you can lean on. Inside, the air is still and bright and wrong. The locals call the calm the Lull, and they whisper, because the wall listens.

monsters.name: Eye-wall sentinel
monsters.lore: One of the Queen's own watch, half weather itself. It does not roar; thunder does that for it, on cue.

monsters.name: Lull courtier
monsters.lore: Her Majesty knows you are here. What remains to be decided is the manner of your arrival — walking, or delivered.

monsters.name: Pressure-ghost
monsters.lore: A climber the storm took, worn down to a pressure change with a grudge. Your lungs notice it before your eyes do.

monsters.name: Rain hound
monsters.lore: The Queen kennels the squalls that behave. This one behaves right up until the leash comes off.

runt.tag: gaunt and limping — an easy kill, thin pickings

tough.tag: scarred and heavy-set — dangerous, but it will pay

alpha.tag: an alpha, twice the size — worth a fortune or a funeral

floors.description: Inside the eye the Queen keeps court on a floating ring of wrecked flagships, rigging strung with captured lightning. Harpies in livery, drakes on perches, weather bowing in and out. On the throne of masthead and storm-glass, someone is expecting you.

monsters.name: Queen's champion drake
monsters.lore: It fights before the throne, which means it fights beautifully, which does not mean it fights fair.

monsters.name: Court guard harpy
monsters.lore: Protocol requires all challengers to arrive bleeding. The court dislikes ambiguity; the pike and the plate remove it.

monsters.name: Unbottled gale
monsters.lore: Bottled since the fleet fell, dropped the way courts do accidents. It holds you personally responsible.

monsters.name: Perch squire
monsters.lore: A groom of the court perches, armed with the champion's second-best gorget and none of its patience.

runt.tag: gaunt and limping — an easy kill, thin pickings

tough.tag: scarred and heavy-set — dangerous, but it will pay

alpha.tag: an alpha, twice the size — worth a fortune or a funeral

floors.description: Above the storm the tower goes quiet. A forest floor with no sky — black boughs closing overhead, and under them a dusk that never ripens into night. The gate town keeps one lamp lit facing the trees, and the trees keep their distance. Mostly.

monsters.name: Eaves shade
monsters.lore: It is thrown ahead of you by no light at all, and when you stop, it keeps walking. Spells pass through what isn't there.

monsters.name: Gloom hound
monsters.lore: The Huntsman's stock run loose between hunts, keeping themselves fed. The downwind circle is habit it does not need.

monsters.name: Dead signal
monsters.lore: The old realm's transmissions never died here. They just kept walking, and one of them knows your name.

monsters.name: Dusk boar
monsters.lore: It roots the treeline where the lamplight fails, and it has decided the failing light is its property.

runt.tag: gaunt and limping — an easy kill, thin pickings

tough.tag: scarred and heavy-set — dangerous, but it will pay

alpha.tag: an alpha, twice the size — worth a fortune or a funeral

floors.description: The trees here carry sound the way wires carry charge. Every word spoken here keeps traveling, trunk to trunk, for years — the wood is full of conversations that outlived both parties. The locals trade in whispers and go armed against being quoted.

monsters.name: Quoted shade
monsters.lore: It finishes sentences said here long ago in your voice, and it knows things you said three floors down. It has had time to take them personally.

monsters.name: Echo hound
monsters.lore: It throws its own footfalls ahead of itself. You hear it pass on the left. That is where it is not.

monsters.name: Stray nightmare
monsters.lore: Saddled in cobweb, patient. It has never needed to chase — everyone in the gate town knows somebody who got on.

monsters.name: Gall wasps
monsters.lore: They nest in the talking trees and sting whatever raises its voice. The wood has opinions about being quoted.

runt.tag: gaunt and limping — an easy kill, thin pickings

tough.tag: scarred and heavy-set — dangerous, but it will pay

alpha.tag: an alpha, twice the size — worth a fortune or a funeral

floors.description: Long straight avenues cut through the black forest, grassed in grey. These are the Huntsman's rides, and everything in the Gloom knows their calendar. On hunt nights the towns bar their doors. Between hunts, the rides are the fastest road north.

monsters.name: Ride-warden hound
monsters.lore: You are game, walking the master's ride. The one low note is it logging the flush.

monsters.name: Grey outrider
monsters.lore: One of the Huntsman's whips, grey from hat to boot. The lean as it passes is a fitting — for the next hunt's card.

monsters.name: Verge-runner shade
monsters.lore: Once quarry, still running the verge on hunt nights, unable to stop. Behind it the ride goes cold, remembering.

monsters.name: Ride crow
monsters.lore: It follows the hunts the way its kind follow armies, and it has learned the calendar better than the towns.

runt.tag: gaunt and limping — an easy kill, thin pickings

tough.tag: scarred and heavy-set — dangerous, but it will pay

alpha.tag: an alpha, twice the size — worth a fortune or a funeral

floors.description: Clearings open in the forest, and each one holds a moment that will not finish — a wedding dance, a skirmish, played over in grey light with the sound worn off. The realm's last transmissions pooled in these glades when the signal died. Walk around them.

monsters.name: The dancers
monsters.lore: The round has a gap where someone used to be, and every grey face turns to you with the same polite, starving expectation.

monsters.name: Skirmish remnant
monsters.lore: After all these years it has noticed the enemy stopped coming. It is relieved beyond words to have somebody real.

monsters.name: Glade-shy hound
monsters.lore: The hounds will not enter the glades, which tells you something. It drives travelers in instead, patient as a sheepdog.

monsters.name: Glade moth
monsters.lore: It feeds on the grey light of the replays, and it resents every shadow that dims the show.

runt.tag: gaunt and limping — an easy kill, thin pickings

tough.tag: scarred and heavy-set — dangerous, but it will pay

alpha.tag: an alpha, twice the size — worth a fortune or a funeral

floors.description: The forest opens onto meadows of black grass under a paper-grey sky, and the meadows are pasture. The Huntsman's nightmares graze between hunts — a herd, coal-dark, cropping grass that whispers. The herd-boys of Wickstead never, under anything, run.

monsters.name: Grazing nightmare
monsters.lore: Whatever it dreams while it grazes, you have just walked into it, and it objects.

monsters.name: Herd stallion
monsters.lore: A tower of black muscle and slow smoke. It puts itself between you and the herd and hopes you will insist — you will not wear it down before dark.

monsters.name: Pasture hound
monsters.lore: Chosen for patience. It watched you cross half a mile of meadow without moving. Now it moves.

monsters.name: Black crake
monsters.lore: It nests in the whispering grass and screams the herd's alarms. The herd-boys hate it more than the herd.

runt.tag: gaunt and limping — an easy kill, thin pickings

tough.tag: scarred and heavy-set — dangerous, but it will pay

alpha.tag: an alpha, twice the size — worth a fortune or a funeral

floors.description: An avenue of statues runs through the forest — the realm's heroes in bronze, every one missing its shadow. The shadows walk the avenue on their own now, trading plinths. The gate town sells candles by the dozen: a lit candle owns its shadow. Yours.

monsters.name: Unfixed shadow
monsters.lore: A century drilled into the bronze made the stance flawless. It fights like the statue's better memory of itself, and blows ring on it like metal.

monsters.name: Candle-thief shade
monsters.lore: It pinches out flames down the avenue, and your circle of light is next on the round.

monsters.name: Avenue hound
monsters.lore: Its shadow does not match — too big, walking on the walls. When the hound stops, the shadow keeps coming.

monsters.name: Avenue rat
monsters.lore: It eats the candle-stubs the pilgrims leave and has grown bold enough to prefer them lit.

runt.tag: gaunt and limping — an easy kill, thin pickings

tough.tag: scarred and heavy-set — dangerous, but it will pay

alpha.tag: an alpha, twice the size — worth a fortune or a funeral

floors.description: The Huntsman kennels his pack in a ruined manor court, and the court has grown to fit the pack — gates of black bone, a mews where winged things shift in the dark. The kennel-shades keep the feeding book fastidiously. Do not read the entries.

monsters.name: Kennel-master shade
monsters.lore: It looks you over as stock, checks the feeding book, and unclips the first lead. The apron has seen use.

monsters.name: Pack matron
monsters.lore: She does not run with the hunts anymore; she trains what does. The whole court goes quiet to watch the lesson.

monsters.name: Mews-kept nightmare
monsters.lore: Stabled for re-breaking, and the door is open again. It wears its freedom like a dare.

monsters.name: Mews owl
monsters.lore: The winged things in the mews are hooded for a reason. This one worked its hood off.

runt.tag: gaunt and limping — an easy kill, thin pickings

tough.tag: scarred and heavy-set — dangerous, but it will pay

alpha.tag: an alpha, twice the size — worth a fortune or a funeral

floors.description: The forest here has been dressed — every path a lane, every lane a funnel, every funnel ending somewhere prepared. Snares of shadow and wire, a tree that is a trigger. The Huntsman does not always ride his quarry down. Sometimes he prefers it delivered.

monsters.name: Snare-setter
monsters.lore: It weaves shadow through wire with a craftsman's absorption. You are the test of the workmanship.

monsters.name: The caught thing
monsters.lore: Cutting it down is mercy. Mercy, out here, has a survival rate.

monsters.name: Funnel hound
monsters.lore: Never closing, only steering. Ahead the trees narrow. You are being delivered, on schedule.

monsters.name: Wire beetle
monsters.lore: It eats the Huntsman's snare-wire and armors itself with the leavings. The snare-setters bill it as an occupational hazard.

runt.tag: gaunt and limping — an easy kill, thin pickings

tough.tag: scarred and heavy-set — dangerous, but it will pay

alpha.tag: an alpha, twice the size — worth a fortune or a funeral

floors.description: The last stretch before the Pale Court is where the Huntsman runs his best game, and the forest has been worn into racecourse — banked turns of black turf, hides for an audience. Tonight's card has one name on it. Bayhollow has already placed its bets.

monsters.name: Pacing hound
monsters.lore: It is not hunting. It is pacing you, for the handicap, and it keeps glancing at your knees.

monsters.name: Rival quarry
monsters.lore: Three hunts' worth of broken snares hang off it. Thinning the competition counts as strategy.

monsters.name: Course steward
monsters.lore: You are off the marked course. Rejoining is compulsory. The flag is not a request.

monsters.name: Stand crow
monsters.lore: It works the audience hides for dropped stakes and settles bets nobody survived to collect.

runt.tag: gaunt and limping — an easy kill, thin pickings

tough.tag: scarred and heavy-set — dangerous, but it will pay

alpha.tag: an alpha, twice the size — worth a fortune or a funeral

floors.description: The forest ends at a hall with no walls — pale columns of birch bone, a floor of grey turf, a sky the color of a held breath. Hounds in their hundreds sit the perimeter in silence. The hunt is assembled, and at its head, horn in hand, waits the master.

monsters.name: The first whip
monsters.lore: Precedence must be observed — nobody reaches the master unbloodied. The lash uncoils with the boredom of long practice.

monsters.name: Brace of pale hounds
monsters.lore: White as the columns, moving in mirrored arcs. They have opened every hunt for a century. They open yours.

monsters.name: The master's remount
monsters.lore: The master's spare, saddle empty. It considers the vacancy an insult and comes to fill the time.

monsters.name: Unblooded hound
monsters.lore: Too young for the perimeter's silence, it breaks rank for you — its first hunt, and it wants it perfect.

floors.description: The Gloom's last trees stand against a wall of black iron, and the wall goes up out of sight. The King's first outwork: ramparts of welded plate, gun-slits that breathe, a gate scaled for siege engines. Some of this wall was not built. It grew.

monsters.name: Outwork imp
monsters.lore: Maintenance doubles as sentry duty out here. It reports you with the rivet gun.

monsters.name: Hellknight of the gate
monsters.lore: Armor welded shut a lifetime ago, engine-heart idling up through the plate. The halberd is part of the arm.

monsters.name: Wall-flesh
monsters.lore: The outwork's living mortar. The wall behind it heals over before it has crossed half the distance.

monsters.name: Outwork crow
monsters.lore: Iron walls still feed crows. The gun-slits breathe out, and something always rides the warm draft.

floors.description: The chains that bind every stolen realm were forged here, and the yards never stopped — acre after acre of anvils, quench-pits of black oil, chain running overhead. The hammer rhythm is constant. The locals set their hearts by it, having no choice.

monsters.name: Chain-gang imp
monsters.lore: The foreman has spotted a way to lighten the load — you look sturdy, and the harness is adjustable.

monsters.name: Quench-tempered knight
monsters.lore: Fresh from tempering, issued nothing yet but the need to test itself.

monsters.name: Living chain
monsters.lore: The forge puts a little of the fire into everything it makes. This one got a temper.

monsters.name: Quench-pit eel
monsters.lore: It swims the black oil between temperings and eats what the quench rejects. Spellwork slicks off it with the oil.

floors.description: Roads of grated iron run between the outworks, laid over open furnace channels — the March's blood-heat, piped floor to floor. Walking them means walking on light. The furnaces below are fed by chute, and it is bad luck to ask what the chutes are fed.

monsters.name: Stoker imp
monsters.lore: The furnace is running lean, the schedule says feed it, and you are standing on the hatch — which counts as volunteering.

monsters.name: Road-warden knight
monsters.lore: It patrols the grate barefoot, soles glowing dull red. Heat discipline is a point of pride, and it means to teach the standard.

monsters.name: Under-grate thing
monsters.lore: It lives between the furnaces, eating what the chutes deliver. It has learned the sound of footsteps stopping, and spells cook off before they reach it.

monsters.name: Cinder swift
monsters.lore: It nests in the road grating and hunts the updraft. Nothing else on the March flies this low on purpose.

floors.description: This is where the King's army is made, and it is not recruited. Halls of surgical gantries run to the horizon, arc-light flickering off hanging plate. Flesh goes in at one door. What comes out the other door marches. The halls are always working.

monsters.name: Seam-checker imp
monsters.lore: It taps you twice, frowns at the sound of unmodified meat, and flags you for the gantries.

monsters.name: Fresh-welded soldier
monsters.lore: It does not know its own name yet. It knows its function, and its function is walking toward you.

monsters.name: The rejected lot
monsters.lore: The failures have organized — wrong joints, extra arms, grievances in writing.

monsters.name: Arc moth
monsters.lore: It drinks the welding light. The gantry crews bill the King for what it costs them in torches.

floors.description: Between the great works, the March's labor force lives in a city of its own making — a slum of flue-pipes and stolen plate, stacked twelve deep, riddled with markets and feuds. A million imps, more or less. Everything is for sale, including the etiquette.

monsters.name: Warren tough
monsters.lore: A glandular marvel, the locals say. You are new custom, walking unprotected.

monsters.name: Warren press-gang
monsters.lore: The Welding Halls pay a bounty per body, and yours is worth a month of quota. It is nothing personal. It is documented.

monsters.name: Off-duty hellknight
monsters.lore: Retired into the warrens, rent collected in teeth. It is sure beyond argument that you owe it something.

monsters.name: Flue bat
monsters.lore: A million chimneys, one bat per flue. The warrens sell the guano and lose the arguments.

floors.description: Nine bastions in echelon, each one a fortress that would anchor a kingdom's border below, here just a rung. The garrisons drill day and night against an enemy the officers will not name. It is you. The drill instructors use your description.

monsters.name: Drill-square knight
monsters.lore: It has rehearsed this fight so long it starts with your counter.

monsters.name: Ballista crew
monsters.lore: Their record on moving targets is chalked on the wall. It is embarrassing, and they know you can read it.

monsters.name: Parade hulk
monsters.lore: Polished for parades, at attention for a decade, waiting for an order worth having. Your arrival is an order — and it was built to be impossible to stop.

monsters.name: Rampart falcon
monsters.lore: The garrisons fly messages between bastions. The falcons have standing orders about interceptors.

monsters.name: Sally hound
monsters.lore: Kenneled at the sally ports and fed on drill-square mistakes. It knows the gap in every formation.

floors.description: The King grows his siege engines. Rows of them stand planted in beds of bone-meal and engine oil — rams budding off trellises, trebuchets ripening on the stem. Imp gardeners work the rows. The harvest is scheduled for the war after this one.

monsters.name: Pruning-torch imp
monsters.lore: Contamination of the beds is the one sin the head gardener flogs for, and you are tracking in pollen from ninety floors of elsewhere.

monsters.name: Unripe engine
monsters.lore: Green, unbalanced, and eager — a colt with a battering head, ruining the rows to reach you.

monsters.name: Garden scarecrow
monsters.lore: The gardeners forgot to tell it the war it fell in is over. It comes off the frame with the nails still in.

monsters.name: Carrion kite
monsters.lore: What the scarecrow is for. It has been testing the scarecrow's patience for years, and yours looks shorter.

floors.description: The March keeps its faith in chapels of riveted iron, and the faith is the King. Bells of engine-block, choirs of exhaust, litanies in a script that moves when read. The furnace-priests preach the Ascent in reverse: everything descends, eventually.

monsters.name: Furnace-priest
monsters.lore: It has preached your arrival for years and would hate to waste the congregation. The litany turns spellwork back like heat off a firebox.

monsters.name: Choir imp
monsters.lore: Heresy duty is the only part of the liturgy they enjoy, and you are unmistakably not in the hymnal.

monsters.name: Penitent hellknight
monsters.lore: Chained to the pew by its own request. Absolution, in the March, is worked off in single combat.

monsters.name: Censer haunt
monsters.lore: Enough coal-smoke has been swung at the King's name that some of it stayed to listen.

floors.description: The last road is a triumphal way built for one commuter: Malgrim, the King's voice, whose processions descend when a realm is to be told it has fallen. The road is lined with the honor guard, at their posts tonight. You are the procession now.

monsters.name: Honor guard knight
monsters.lore: Nine climbers' names recited as introduction and warning. The speech-runed plate has turned everything they tried.

monsters.name: Banner-bearer imp
monsters.lore: It refuses, absolutely, to set the banner down — the banner is the post.

monsters.name: Proclamation hulk
monsters.lore: The proclamation is your death notice, read in advance, at a volume that loosens rivets.

monsters.name: Horn bat
monsters.lore: It roosts in the proclamation horns between readings. The readings have made it deaf and fearless.

floors.description: The March ends at a gate of black iron scaled for a god, and before it, a parade ground where the King's herald holds court over the Marshals of the March. The banners are silent. Malgrim has dismissed the guard — a courtesy, to you and to the guard.

monsters.name: Marshal of the March
monsters.lore: Presenting the Herald with your head might be worth the flogging. It has done the arithmetic, visibly, and closed the ledger.

monsters.name: The Herald's secretary
monsters.lore: Fat and precise on state secrets, carrying a pre-signed writ of execution. Spells blur against what it knows and will not say.

monsters.name: Gate-tender hulk
monsters.lore: One duty and no discretion — nothing passes while the Herald holds court. It has the patience and the build of architecture.

monsters.name: Muster hound
monsters.lore: It runs the parade ground's edge at every muster. Dismissing the guard did not dismiss the dog.

monsters.name: Drummer imp
monsters.lore: The muster-beat must be kept while the gate stands. Nobody told it the muster was over.

floors.description: Above the March there is no more pretense of country. The Crown is one building — black glass grown around the tower's reactor-heart — and this floor is its doorstep: a stair of obsidian, polished mirror-deep. Your reflection arrives first. It reports.

monsters.name: Obsidian sentinel
monsters.lore: The Crown does not garrison its doorstep with soldiers. It casts them, and glass casts thick.

monsters.name: Your reflection
monsters.lore: It wears your stance, your gear, and a much better night's sleep. Spells recognize themselves in it and hesitate.

monsters.name: Court page
monsters.lore: Refusing a royal summons is death. Accepting is death with better lighting. It waits, professionally, while you choose.

monsters.name: Mirror moth
monsters.lore: It lays its eggs in reflections. The stair-keepers polish against it, and lose ground yearly.

floors.description: The citadel's outer halls are walled in polished obsidian, and the court uses them the way courts use mirrors — for vanity, and for watching behind themselves. Every surface holds a crowd of reflections, and not all of them have owners present.

monsters.name: Gallery duelist
monsters.lore: A century against its own reflection, and the reflection finally let it win. Dueling here is how the court says hello.

monsters.name: Orphaned reflection
monsters.lore: Its owner died at some forgotten intrigue. It has found a body it likes, and spells slide off the glass it lives behind.

monsters.name: Whispering courtier
monsters.lore: All silk and sympathy until the third sentence, when the sympathy runs out and the silk turns out to be wire.

monsters.name: Sconce imp
monsters.lore: It tends the gallery lamps and taxes every shadow they throw. Yours arrived unregistered.

floors.description: The citadel's walls go translucent here, and you see what the Crown is built around: the reactor-heart, a column of caged light climbing the floors like a spine. Its hum is in your teeth. The keepers wear crowns of lead and do not take questions.

monsters.name: Lead-crowned engineer
monsters.lore: Interruptions to the great work are bled off like excess pressure. Under the lead and the smoked glass, almost nothing gets through.

monsters.name: Light-leak
monsters.lore: A thread of the heart's light that learned to move against the draft, feeling for something to be inside.

monsters.name: Coil-fed demon
monsters.lore: Jaw wired straight into the shielding, radiant with theft. It should not be here either, which makes you a witness.

monsters.name: Sluice rat
monsters.lore: It nests in the reactor shielding, warm and half-bright, and defends the warmth like a birthright.

floors.description: A floor of waiting rooms, because even a demon court runs on waiting. Petitioners from a hundred conquered realms sit the benches — some for decades, some past being alive, all holding numbered tokens of black glass. A token is issued. The token is warm.

monsters.name: Queue veteran
monsters.lore: It has waited so long it became part of the protocol — robes fused to the stone, token worn smooth. You will tire before it does; everyone has.

monsters.name: Under-chamberlain
monsters.lore: Your paperwork is fatally out of order. The regret is genuine. The fatality is procedural.

monsters.name: Recalled tokens
monsters.lore: A century of the queue, voided, and the recalled tokens want their holders. Yours is getting warmer.

monsters.name: Petitioner's hound
monsters.lore: Its master's number was never called. It holds the bench, and the grudge, on his behalf.

floors.description: The King keeps what he takes, curated: the crown jewels of drowned realms, a carousel from somewhere that surrendered too late. Every exhibit is labeled, honestly, in the court script. Near the stair stands an empty plinth, pre-labeled.

monsters.name: The curator
monsters.lore: It knows the provenance of everything in the vaults, including the piece the empty plinth is waiting for.

monsters.name: Exhibit, awake
monsters.lore: A realm's champion, taken whole, armor and all. Its terrible question: which side of a plinth are you on?

monsters.name: Court appraiser
monsters.lore: Your gear disappoints it. Your defiance, it says, brightening, will mount beautifully.

monsters.name: Case moth
monsters.lore: It eats the exhibits — tapestry first, provenance second. The curator has posted a bounty in three scripts.

floors.description: The court takes its air in gardens grown from every realm the King broke — elven lamp-trees grafted onto dwarven iron-roses, meadow turf from floor one. Nothing here grows the way it did at home. Everything grows.

monsters.name: Grafted horror
monsters.lore: Somewhere inside it is a cutting of the forest from floor twenty- three, and it remembers you passing. The graft drinks spellwork like lamp-oil.

monsters.name: Keeper of the beds
monsters.lore: You are standing on the floor-one turf. It is very rare. It is very rare because of people like you.

monsters.name: Night-pollen drift
monsters.lore: What it pollinates, the gardeners harvest. Do not inhale the future.

monsters.name: Iron-rose beetle
monsters.lore: It feeds on the dwarven iron-roses and grows its shell from the clippings. The gardeners call it a pest with tenure.

floors.description: The processional road to the throne begins here — an avenue of black glass lined with the banners of every realm, hung upside down. Court law says the Kingsway may be walked only in procession. It has waited ninety-six floors for you to break it.

monsters.name: Herald of precedence
monsters.lore: Processions require rank, and rank requires patents, and you have neither — only, it allows, a certain momentum.

monsters.name: Banner-wraith
monsters.lore: The flag of a dead realm flying itself, looking for hands to carry it right side up. Yours are occupied. It intends to free them.

monsters.name: Kingsway guard
monsters.lore: They have drilled the arrest of an unauthorized walker every day for a thousand years. You can tell — and the plate has drilled with them.

monsters.name: Kingsway hound
monsters.lore: The road-watch runs hounds down the avenue between processions. Unauthorized walkers are their whole diet.

floors.description: The court settles everything here, on a floor of black glass scored with a thousand years of measured paces. The galleries are full — word of you has climbed faster than you have. Tonight's card was cleared by royal order. The court has bet heavily anyway.

monsters.name: Champion of the lower court
monsters.lore: It salutes the royal box first, you second — protocol, and also a tell. It has never once been allowed to lose.

monsters.name: The arbiter
monsters.lore: No patents, no second, no grave-plot reserved — irregular. The penalty is assessed in the traditional currency, on the spot.

monsters.name: A settled wager
monsters.lore: It stands to lose a province on how far you get, and it has come over the rail to adjust the outcome personally.

monsters.name: Chalk page
monsters.lore: It scores the measures into the glass before every duel. The floor's thousand years of lines are its one work.

floors.description: One floor remains, and it is mostly door — the King's own, tall enough that clouds form against it. Before it camps the court's conscience — all the demons who came this far meaning to knock, and did not. They watch you cross their camp in silence.

monsters.name: Knight of the threshold camp
monsters.lore: If you knock, its hundred years of not-knocking become cowardice. It cannot allow the redefinition. The plate has camped as long as the doubt.

monsters.name: The last tempter
monsters.lore: The offer is genuine. That is the trap — there is nothing dishonest to push against, and spells find nothing dishonest to bite.

monsters.name: Acolyte of the door
monsters.lore: The door must not be touched by the unworthy, and its test of worth is administered by hand, immediately.

monsters.name: Threshold raven
monsters.lore: It has watched the camp not-knock for a century, and it heckles every new arrival's resolve.

tough.tag: scarred and heavy-set — dangerous, but it will pay

floors.description: The throne room is the reactor, and the reactor is the throne — one chamber where the stolen world's weight hangs in chains of light from a single black seat. The court is assembled. The realms watch through every mirror. The King rises to meet you himself.

monsters.name: The assembled court
monsters.lore: They fight the way courts do: all at once, and each hoping the others die doing it.

monsters.name: The King's shadow
monsters.lore: A younger King, and hungrier, and it does not answer to the one on the throne.

monsters.name: The living regalia
monsters.lore: Scepter, orb, and chain of office in slow orbit. They have outlasted four bearers and are auditioning the fifth, armed.

monsters.name: Mirror witness
monsters.lore: Every conquered realm watches the throne room through its mirrors. One of them could not keep watching quietly.
